Edo period.fact: The Edo period, also called the Tokugawa period, is the period between 1600 or 1603 and 1868 in the history of Japan, when the country was under the rule of the Tokugawa shogunate and some 300 regional daimyo, or feudal lords. Eighty Years' War, 1566–1572.question: Philippe III de Croÿ, the Duke of _____, had been Orange's rival before Alba's 1567 arrival, and he became the de facto leader of his majesty's loyal opposition in the years thereafter (1567–1576)
Eighty Years' War, 1566–1572.fact: Philippe III de Croÿ, the Duke of Aarschot, had been Orange's rival before Alba's 1567 arrival, and he became the de facto leader of his majesty's loyal opposition in the years thereafter (1567–1576). It was not until the Spanish Fury that their interests firmly coincided, and Orange and Aarschot became allies in their joint rebellion against the king.
